answer: No. The assessment does not treat 800 sq ft as a universal cap. It applies 800 sq ft as the maximum for one specific path: the state-exempt detached ADU branch (Gov. Code § 66323(a)(2)), which also uses four-foot side and rear setbacks and a 16/18/20 ft height limit. The assessment says larger ADUs fall under a separate local-ordinance branch. It also says explicitly that it is not claiming every larger local ADU is prohibited. However, it did not evaluate that local-ordinance branch. So it cannot say whether a larger ADU would be allowed on this property, or under what size, setback or height limits. Your current project input of 750 sq ft is within the 800 sq ft maximum for the state-exempt branch. This is an interpretation of the source with medium confidence, not a permit determination.

There is no height limit contained in State ADU Law, but local agencies may impose height
limits pursuant to Government Code section 66321, subdivision (b)(4). A local agency may

A local agency may not impose a height limit that is less than the following:

Detached ADUs

16 feet on a lot with a proposed or existing single-family or multifamily dwelling unit (Gov.
